nexusClaim.associationBasis: Authoring registers this relationship only as the population-level association the located hepatocellular-carcinoma literature supports: sarcopenia is common in HCC (pooled prevalence 42 percent, 95 percent CI 0.36-0.48, across 48 studies and 8,959 patients, with muscle mass CT-assessed at the third lumbar vertebra in 47 of the 48 — 43 skeletal-muscle index and four psoas — with one MRI-derived FFMA study and each study's original definition and cut-point retained, PMID 37274463; pooled prevalence 39 percent, 95 percent CI 33-45 percent, across 42 studies and 8,445 patients pooling six assessment methods — CT-based SMI, PMI, TPV, TPMT/BH and IMAC and MRI-derived FFMA, PMID 36590214) and is independently associated with shorter overall survival (pooled adjusted HR 1.84, 95 percent CI 1.62-2.09) and shorter progression-free survival (pooled HR 1.33, 95 percent CI 1.12-1.56) irrespective of treatment modality (PMID 36590214); the 90-patient curative-intent cohort found sarcopenia in 57.8 percent with median overall survival 33 versus 105 months (P=0.002) and adjusted HR 3.756 (P=0.001), but NO disease-free-survival difference, and attributed the survival gap mainly to treatment-related mortality (17.3 versus 2.6 percent) and major complications (32.7 versus 13.2 percent) (PMID 26266324). The registered claim is co-occurrence and prognostic association at population level only, in established HCC populations, and intentionally not beyond them.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR 3.310 is established for any individual by these anchors: all three measured muscle mass or its prognostic correlates rather than etiology, are predominantly retrospective or aggregate predominantly retrospective cohorts, and do not separate tumor-driven muscle loss from cirrhosis, alcohol exposure, aging, nutrition or treatment effects; the cohort anchor's survival signal ran mainly through major complications and treatment-related mortality rather than through disease-free survival. Individual claims require a documented HCC diagnosis and treatment timeline, a reproducible CT muscle-mass measurement with its stated threshold, assessment of cirrhosis severity and alcohol exposure, exclusion of cachexia-dominant wasting and independent nutritional disease, and qualified clinical opinion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: The hypothesized cascade runs from hepatocellular-carcinoma disease burden, its cirrhotic liver substrate and its treatments through anorexia, hypermetabolism and systemic inflammation to net skeletal-muscle catabolism; no located anchor isolates that cascade in an individual, so the vector is stated as hypothesized rather than established.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Where cirrhosis coexists, portosystemic shunting, protein-calorie malnutrition and alcohol exposure independently drive muscle loss, and the located cancer-population anchors do not separate those drives from the tumor itself.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY on two systematic reviews and one curative-intent cohort, all in established hepatocellular-carcinoma populations, and intentionally not beyond them. The registered claim is population-level co-occurrence and prognostic association only: sarcopenia is common in HCC (pooled prevalence 42 percent, 95 percent CI 0.36-0.48, 48 studies and 8,959 patients, with muscle mass CT-assessed at the third lumbar vertebra in 47 of the 48 — 43 skeletal-muscle index and four psoas — with one MRI-derived FFMA study and each study's original definition and cut-point retained, PMID 37274463; pooled prevalence 39 percent, 95 percent CI 33-45 percent, 42 studies and 8,445 patients pooling six assessment methods — CT-based SMI, PMI, TPV, TPMT/BH and IMAC and MRI-derived FFMA, PMID 36590214) and is independently associated with shorter overall survival (pooled adjusted HR 1.84, 95 percent CI 1.62-2.09) and shorter progression-free survival (pooled HR 1.33, 95 percent CI 1.12-1.56) irrespective of treatment modality (PMID 36590214); the 90-patient curative-intent cohort found sarcopenia in 57.8 percent with median overall survival 33 versus 105 months (P=0.002) and adjusted HR 3.756 (P=0.001), but no disease-free-survival difference, and attributed the survival gap mainly to treatment-related mortality (17.3 versus 2.6 percent) and major complications (32.7 versus 13.2 percent) (PMID 26266324). Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR 3.310 is established for any individual: the anchors measured muscle mass rather than etiology, are predominantly retrospective, and do not separate tumor-driven loss from cirrhosis, alcohol exposure, aging, nutrition or treatment effects. Individual claims require a documented HCC diagnosis and treatment timeline, a reproducible CT muscle-mass measurement with its stated threshold, assessment of cirrhosis severity and alcohol exposure, exclusion of cachexia-dominant wasting and independent nutritional disease, and qualified clinical opinion. The three anchors completed qualified-human citation verification on 2026-10-04 under docs/citation-verification-sop.md, with a recorded narrowing of the two pooled prevalence anchors' assessment-method description to the composition their full texts report (see docs/liver-cancer-sarcopenia-citation-verification-2026-disposition.md); the adjacency edge authored on 2026-10-03 and this authored-corpus registration, which landed the same day under Stage 3b of the signed design, carry the same conservative framing.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Definition and design heterogeneity: the anchors define sarcopenia by CT-derived muscle-mass indices (one pooled prevalence study MRI-derived; the prognostic synthesis pools six CT- and MRI-based methods) whose thresholds and measurement levels vary across the pooled studies, and none of the located anchors separates sarcopenia from cancer cachexia, so a cachectic patient can be counted as sarcopenic and vice versa; the meta-analyses aggregate mostly retrospective cohorts and were not designed to establish individual etiology or onset chronology; the cohort anchor found no disease-free-survival difference, so its overall-survival signal runs mainly through major complications (32.7 versus 13.2 percent) and treatment-related mortality (17.3 versus 2.6 percent), which are treatment consequences rather than registered secondary conditions; pooled prevalence is higher in studies with a high proportion of male patients (45 versus 37 percent) and in younger patients (46 versus 39 percent), so sex- and age-specific applicability is not uniform; and body weight cannot rule the phenotype out because muscle mass, not weight, is measured.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Decompensated cirrhosis or chronic liver disease itself, which independently produces sarcopenia and is present in most hepatocellular-carcinoma populations
Cancer cachexia, a distinct systemic inflammation-dominant wasting syndrome that the located anchors do not separate from sarcopenia
Alcohol use disorder and ongoing alcohol exposure as a rival metabolic and muscle-toxic driver
Age-related primary sarcopenia, deconditioning and physical inactivity independent of the tumor
Treatment effects of resection, ablation, locoregional therapy and systemic therapy, which are treatments and not secondary conditions and independently reduce muscle mass
Nutritional insufficiency, malabsorption, anorexia or fasting related to illness rather than to tumor-driven catabolism

evidenceGaps: No located anchor separates tumor-driven muscle loss from cirrhosis, alcohol exposure, aging, nutrition or treatment effects; the meta-analyses are aggregations of mostly retrospective cohorts and do not establish individual etiology or onset chronology.

Sarcopenia is defined by CT-derived muscle-mass indices (one pooled prevalence study MRI-derived; the prognostic synthesis pools six CT- and MRI-based methods) whose thresholds and measurement levels vary across the pooled studies, and none of the located anchors separates sarcopenia from cancer cachexia, so the two phenotypes can overlap within the counted populations.

The cohort anchor found no disease-free-survival difference, so its overall-survival signal runs mainly through major complications (32.7 versus 13.2 percent) and treatment-related mortality (17.3 versus 2.6 percent), which are treatment consequences rather than registered secondary conditions.

Pooled prevalence is higher in studies with a high proportion of male patients (45 versus 37 percent) and in younger patients (46 versus 39 percent), so sex- and age-specific applicability is not uniform.
Body weight does not exclude the phenotype: the anchors measure CT muscle mass, so normal or high BMI with low muscle mass (myopenic obesity) remains within the counted population.
suggestions.rationale: Authoring registers the signed liver-cancer to sarcopenia route (docs/catalog-identity-migration-design-2026-09-29.md) into the authored corpus under the design's Stage 3b, locking this suggestion to the adjacency layer's first real authored edge, which landed together with the sarcopenia identity addition that makes its target a catalog member. The located evidence quantifies both burden and prognostic association in established hepatocellular-carcinoma populations: pooled sarcopenia prevalence is 42 percent across 48 studies and 8,959 patients (muscle mass CT-assessed at the third lumbar vertebra in 47 of the 48 — 43 skeletal-muscle index and four psoas — with one MRI-derived FFMA study and each study's original definition and cut-point retained; PMID 37274463) and 39 percent across 42 studies and 8,445 patients pooling six assessment methods (CT-based SMI, PMI, TPV, TPMT/BH and IMAC and MRI-derived FFMA; PMID 36590214), with pooled adjusted overall-survival HR 1.84 and progression-free-survival HR 1.33 (PMID 36590214), and the 90-patient curative-intent cohort found sarcopenia in 57.8 percent with median overall survival 33 versus 105 months and adjusted HR 3.756 (PMID 26266324). The edge is deliberately ASSOCIATION_ONLY: no located anchor establishes that liver cancer caused an individual's muscle loss, the cohort's survival signal ran mainly through treatment-related mortality and major complications rather than through disease-free survival, and cirrhosis, alcohol exposure, aging, nutrition and treatment effects remain rival drivers the anchors do not separate. Boundaries carried on the face of the edge: sarcopenia is the muscle-mass and strength syndrome and NOT cancer cachexia, a distinct inflammation-dominant wasting syndrome; body weight does not rule the phenotype in or out because the anchors measure CT muscle mass, so myopenic obesity is within the counted population; and locoregional therapy, resection and systemic therapy are treatments whose complications are not secondary conditions. Direction discipline: every located anchor measures sarcopenia burden or prognosis in established hepatocellular-carcinoma populations; no anchor for the reverse question, whether sarcopenia precedes liver cancer, is registered on this edge. Window discipline: the authored corpus registers liver-cancer to cirrhosis-of-the-liver, so a future cirrhosis-of-the-liver to sarcopenia window would create a direct-versus-chain redundancy conflict that must be adjudicated under npm run audit:crg before authoring; only this single window is authored. The route's anchors (PMID 37274463, PMID 36590214, PMID 26266324) were confirmed absent from the registry and cleared by source-status preflight with zero blocking flags on 2026-10-03; they completed qualified-human citation verification on 2026-10-04, which narrowed the two pooled prevalence anchors' assessment-method description to the composition their full texts report and approved the curative-intent cohort anchor as written (see docs/liver-cancer-sarcopenia-citation-verification-2026-disposition.md), and the relationship row and the three source entities were registered in lockstep with this suggestion on 2026-10-03.

sourceReferences.citation: Liu J, Luo H, Huang L, Wang J. Prevalence of sarcopenia among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Oncol Lett. 2023 Jul;26(1):283. doi:10.3892/ol.2023.13869. PMID 37274463.
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 48 studies and 8,959 patients, registered as this edge's PRIMARY burden anchor: pooled sarcopenia prevalence 42 percent (95 percent CI 0.36-0.48) in hepatocellular-carcinoma populations, with muscle mass CT-assessed at the third lumbar vertebra in 47 of the 48 studies (43 skeletal-muscle index, four psoas) and one study MRI-derived (FFMA), each study's original definition retained because no unanimous standard exists; the abstract reports prevalence higher in studies with a high proportion of male patients (45 versus 37 percent) and in younger patients (46 versus 39 percent), and notes body weight cannot rule the phenotype out because muscle mass is measured. LIMITATIONS CARRIED: definition and threshold heterogeneity across the pooled studies, predominantly retrospective cohorts, and no separation of sarcopenia from cancer cachexia. Qualified-human citation review completed on 2026-10-04: approved with this narrowing to the assessment-method composition the full text reports (pooled prevalence figure unchanged), see docs/liver-cancer-sarcopenia-citation-verification-2026-disposition.md.

LIMITATIONS CARRIED: aggregated mostly retrospective cohorts, no individual etiology or onset chronology, and no separation of sarcopenia from cancer cachexia.
